Shinichiro Tokudome <sup>1</sup>, Yoshihiro Naruo <sup>2</sup>
_Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, Sagamihara-shi, 252-5210, JAPAN_

Hatsuo Mori <sup>3</sup>
_IHI Corporation, Mizuho-machi, 190-1297, JAPAN_

Tsuyoshi Yagishita <sup>4</sup>, and Takayuki Yamamoto <sup>5</sup>
_Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, Sagamihara-shi, 252-5210, JAPAN_

**For a flight test campaign of reusable vehicle, 10 kN class small LOX/LH2 propulsion**
**systems have been developed. They are regenerative cooling engines with a continuous**
**throttling capability for making vertical landing possible. Current phase of the campaign is**
**to demonstrate an entire sequence of full-scale operation with a vehicle equipped with**
**turbopump-fed engine, following the three-generation vehicles with pressure-fed engine had**
**successfully performed in repeated flight operation tests between 1999 and 2003. From a**
**result of primary system analysis, we decided to build an expander cycle engine by**
**refurbishing a pair of turbopumps, which had been build for another research program, and**
**putting them into a new engine developed in the present study. A combustion chamber with**
**long cylindrical portion adapted to the engine cycle was also newly made. Three captive**
**firing tests were conducted to verify functional suitability for the vertical landing flight. In**
**the last two tests, a deep throttling capability down to 28 % and a high-speed response over**
**5 Hz of the propulsion system were successfully demonstrated with newly developed thrust**
**control system. The fourth-generation vehicle powered by the full expander cycle engine is**
**now under development.**

**I.** **Introduction**

The Institute of Space and Astronautical Science of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (ISAS/JAXA) have
been continuing a basic experimental study of future reusable space transportation system, which was named
reusable vehicle testing (RVT), since 1998. A decided target of the study is to develop the system architecture that
makes the transportation cost reduce by two orders of magnitude than it already is. So we built a minicar-sized small
vertical-takeoff-and-landing (VTOL) type vehicle powered by a 10 kN class regenerative cooled liquid oxygen
(LOX) / liquid hydrogen (LH2) propellant rocket engine. The LOX / LH2 propulsion system is a promising candidate
for powering the fully reusable vehicle into space from the viewpoint of minimizing environmental load and
enhancing the feasibility of single-stage-to-orbit (SSTO) concepts. And then, we demonstrated repeated flight
experiments aim at a quick-turnaround operation. Three series of flight experiments had been succeeded with
pressure-fed engine, which had a 5 Hz dynamic response and a deep throttling capability down to 20 % of rated
thrust, for six years from 1998 to 2003 <sup>1, 2</sup> . Figure 1 shows advancement of the test vehicle in RVT campaign. For the
meantime, we had tackled with the challenges in terms of handling of the cryogenic fuel, simplification of the
inspection and maintenance, and enhancement of the lifetime of engine components. An injector and a combustion
chamber had been upgraded by introducing electroforming technique into their production processes in terms of
durability enhancement.

markdown_chunks.section: A High-Speed Response LOX / LH2 Full Expander Cycle Engine with Deep Throttling Capability > Nomenclature
markdown_chunks.text:
The next step for demonstrating entire sequence of full-scale operation is to put a turbopump-fed engine into the
propulsion system. For making the flight tests possible within the realistic limit of the budget, we decided to
refurbish a pair of turbopumps built for another research program and to put them into a new 10 kN class
turbopump-fed engine. A combustion chamber with long cylindrical portion suited to the full expander cycle
concept was newly made by the electroforming technique proven in the former pressure-fed engine. As a result of
the research and development efforts <sup>3</sup> for more than five years, we have completed a full expander cycle engine with
a high-speed dynamic response and a deep throttling capability, which is suited to the fourth generation VTOL
rocket vehicle now under development. This paper describes the results of the design and development of the new
engine with newly proposed thrust control concept.

**II.** **Design Guide for a LOX/LH2 Propulsion System in RVT Campaign**
For RVT campaign, we have designed and developed the LOX/LH2 propulsion systems, which has the
components containing technical challenges as much as possible, in line with the following guidelines.

**A.** **Technical Challenges for Reusable Space Transportation System**

For aiming to develop fully reusable space transportation system, we set the following three technical
challenges: (1) fully reusable propulsion system; (2) use of liquid hydrogen fuel; and (3) achievement of quick
turnaround operation.

For achieving full reusability, the propulsion system would be required higher reliability, durability, and safety
than the expendable one. Additionally, from a viewpoint of operational safety, the handling of liquid hydrogen is
controlled by High Pressure Gas Safety Act (in Japan) and should be pay attention to the characteristics of hydrogen
gas, which diffuses quickly in atmosphere and might form explosive hydrogen-air mixture. Furthermore, the
simplification of hardware components and the minimization of number of items on the inspection and maintenance
lists must be done for achieving the quick repeated flight operation as the key to the reduction of the operational
cost. Meanwhile, we aim to attain fifty times reusability in designing each component.

**B.** **Aims of RVT Campaign**

As activity aims of RVT campaign, we seek to complete the two targets as follows: (1) learning the operational
techniques of reusable propulsion system; and (2) extracting the essential technical challenges in quick repeated
flight operation from the operational testings with the VTOL vehicle.

markdown_chunks.section: A High-Speed Response LOX / LH2 Full Expander Cycle Engine with Deep Throttling Capability > Nomenclature
markdown_chunks.text:
We have to conduct the present study within the realistic limit of the resources for basic research. Therefore, we
decided to minimize the development of new hardware components and to use the existing technology and
components at a maximum. So we have chosen a process to verify the week point of the existing engine components
in the reusable operation, and then to develop the design principle for the components reusable. We need a small test
vehicle, which facilitates a lot of repeated flight tests, for extracting the essential technical challenges from the
issues recognized through operational tests repeated. The vehicle of VTOL style helps our experimental study with
such limitation to perform, since we can conduct the flight test in the narrow flight envelope with small-sized ground
support equipments. In the present activity, the development of the engine system, which has the quick response and
wide range thrust control capability making vertical landing flight possible, is recognized as both the future
technologies applicable to lunar or planetary landers and the essential technical challenges to make our practicalminded basic research a success.

**III.** **Design Consideration of a Turbopump-fed Engine Applicable to Small VTOL vehicle**

There are three requirements for the main propulsion system of the RVT#4 vehicle with turbopump-fed engine:
(1) over 8 kN of rated thrust and continuous throttling capability down to 30 % of the rated thrust for demonstrating
the full-scale operation of the reusable rocket vehicle; (2) over 1 Hz of dynamic thrust control response to meet the
VTOL flight testings within a narrow flight envelope with the small test vehicle; and (3) the preparation and
operation conducted within the realistic limit of the resources for basic research.

markdown_chunks.section: A High-Speed Response LOX / LH2 Full Expander Cycle Engine with Deep Throttling Capability > Nomenclature
markdown_chunks.text:
**A.** **Engine Cycle**

We selected the full expander (FE) engine cycle concept from the viewpoint of enhancing performance, safety,
and operability as the rocket engine which would be applicable to the present research activity. The closed cycle
engine has a relatively higher performance than open cycle’s one, since almost all amount of the propellant is
utilized as the source of propulsive power. In addition, from a result of the primary test, we found that the full
expander cycle engine would be able to stop burning much more safely than the other cycle engines when any
trouble would happen to the engine system itself. Furthermore, ISAS/JAXA has an experience in the development
research of full-scale LOX / LH2 propulsion systems including the expander cycle concept <sup>4, 5</sup> in the 1980s and we
have enough knowledge and skills for developing and operating the propulsion system.
